2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. //==================================================================================================
5. // Imports
6. //==================================================================================================
7. 
8. use vstd::prelude::*;
9. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
10. include!("table.spec.rs");
11. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
12. include!("table.proof.rs");
13. 
14. use super::{
15.     PteWord,
16.     PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2,
17. };
18. 
19. //==================================================================================================
20. // Table Entry Trait
21. //==================================================================================================
22. 
23. ///
24. /// # Description
25. ///
26. /// Trait bound for entry types that can be stored in a page table.
27. ///
28. /// The raw representation uses [`PteWord`] — `u32` on x86.
29. ///
30. pub trait TableEntry: Copy {
31.     /// Creates from a raw [`PteWord`], returning `None` if the value is invalid.
32.     fn from_raw(raw: PteWord) -> Option<Self>;
33.     /// Returns the raw [`PteWord`] representation.
34.     fn raw(self) -> PteWord;
35. }
36. 
37. //==================================================================================================
38. // Table Index
39. //==================================================================================================
40. 
41. ///
42. /// # Description
43. ///
44. /// A validated index into a page table, guaranteed to be in `[0, PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)`.
45. ///
46. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
47. pub struct TableIndex(usize);
48. 
49. impl TableIndex {
50.     ///
51.     /// # Description
52.     ///
53.     /// Creates a [`TableIndex`] from a raw `usize`, returning `None` if the value is out of
54.     /// bounds.
55.     ///
56.     pub const fn new(index: usize) -> Option<Self> {
57.         if index < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH {
58.             Some(Self(index))
59.         } else {
60.             None
61.         }
62.     }
63. 
64.     ///
65.     /// # Description
66.     ///
67.     /// Returns the underlying index value.
68.     ///
69.     pub const fn into_raw(self) -> usize {
70.         self.0
71.     }
72. }
73. 
74. //==================================================================================================
75. // Virtual Address Index Extraction
76. //==================================================================================================
77. 
78. /// Extracts the PD index (bits 22-31) from a virtual address as a [`TableIndex`].
79. pub const fn pd_index(vaddr: usize) -> TableIndex {
80.     // The mask guarantees the result is always < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH.
81.     let index: usize = (vaddr >> crate::mem::PGTAB_SHIFT) & (crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1);
82.     TableIndex(index)
83. }
84. 
85. /// Extracts the PT index (bits 12-21) from a virtual address as a [`TableIndex`].
86. pub const fn pt_index(vaddr: usize) -> TableIndex {
87.     // The mask guarantees the result is always < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH.
88.     let index: usize = (vaddr >> crate::mem::PAGE_SHIFT) & (crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1);
89.     TableIndex(index)
90. }
91. 
92. //==================================================================================================
93. // Table
94. //==================================================================================================
95. 
96. ///
97. /// # Description
98. ///
99. /// A page-table page containing [`PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`](crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH) entries.
100. ///
101. /// This type is parameterized over the entry type to enforce that each table level uses only
102. /// its own entry kind (e.g., PD tables only [`PageDirectoryEntry`], PT tables only
103. /// [`PageTableEntry`]).
104. ///
105. /// The table is accessed via a base address that must be valid in the current address space
106. /// (i.e., a mapped virtual address). It does not own the backing memory — the caller is
107. /// responsible for allocation and lifetime management.
108. ///
109. #[derive(Debug)]
110. pub struct Table<E: TableEntry> {
111.     /// Base address of the table (must be page-aligned).
112.     base: usize,
113.     /// Phantom marker for the entry type.
114.     _marker: ::core::marker::PhantomData<E>,
115. }
116. 
117. impl<E: TableEntry> Table<E> {
118.     ///
119.     /// # Description
120.     ///
121.     /// Creates a table reference from a base address.
122.     ///
123.     /// # Safety
124.     ///
125.     /// `base` must be a valid, page-aligned address with at least one page of readable/writable
126.     /// memory.
127.     ///
128.     pub const unsafe fn from_address(base: usize) -> Self {
129.         Self {
130.             base,
131.             _marker: ::core::marker::PhantomData,
132.         }
133.     }
134. 
135.     ///
136.     /// # Description
137.     ///
138.     /// Reads the entry at `index`.
139.     ///
140.     /// Returns `None` if the raw value is invalid according to `E::from_raw()`.
141.     ///
142.     /// # Safety
143.     ///
144.     /// The memory at `base + index * size_of::<PteWord>()` must be valid for a volatile read.
145.     ///
146.     pub unsafe fn read(&self, index: TableIndex) -> Option<E> {
147.         let offset: usize = index.into_raw() << PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2;
148.         let ptr: *const PteWord = (self.base + offset) as *const PteWord;
149.         E::from_raw(::core::ptr::read_volatile(ptr))
150.     }
151. 
152.     ///
153.     /// # Description
154.     ///
155.     /// Writes `entry` at `index`.
156.     ///
157.     /// # Safety
158.     ///
159.     /// The memory at `base + index * size_of::<PteWord>()` must be valid for a volatile write.
160.     ///
161.     pub unsafe fn write(&self, index: TableIndex, entry: E) {
162.         let offset: usize = index.into_raw() << PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2;
163.         let ptr: *mut PteWord = (self.base + offset) as *mut PteWord;
164.         ::core::ptr::write_volatile(ptr, entry.raw());
165.     }
166. }

6. 2 types (`Table`, `TableIndex`)** and — importantly — **0 external callers for

10. > **Why the script found 0 external callers (false negative).**
11. > This module lives under `src/libs/arch/src/x86/` — the **32-bit x86** build.
12. > rust-analyzer (and thus the script) indexes the **x86_64 host** configuration,
13. > so all real call sites — which are compiled only under `cfg(target_arch =
14. > "x86")` (kernel) or are host-side software page-walkers — are invisible to the
15. > LSP. A textual search across the workspace recovers the true callers below.
16. > Treat the script's "no external callers" warning as a configuration artifact,
17. > **not** as evidence of dead code.

20. `raw`, `Table::read`, `from_raw`, `pt_index`, `TableIndex`, `pd_index`,
21. `Table::from_address`. (`raw`/`from_raw` are the `TableEntry` trait methods,
22. implemented in `pde.rs`/`pte.rs` and dispatched only inside `Table::read`/`write`.)
23. 
24. ## Real Callers (recovered by source search)
25. 
26. ### 1. Kernel identity map — `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs` (primary consumer)
27. 
28. This is the canonical user of the whole module. It walks/builds the kernel's
29. two-level identity map:
30. 
31. - `paging::pd_index(vaddr)` / `paging::pt_index(vaddr)` → `TableIndex`
32.   (L131, L306, L728, L729, L783, L848).
33. - `unsafe { Table::<PageDirectoryEntry>::from_address(pd_paddr) }` and
34.   `Table::<PageTableEntry>::from_address(pt_paddr)` to obtain a typed view over a
35.   physical (identity-mapped) page (L133, L297, L299, L732, L736, L785, L852, L863).
36. - `unsafe { pd.read(pde_idx) }` / `pt.read(pte_idx)` returning
37.   `Option<PageDirectoryEntry>` / `Option<PageTableEntry>`; callers treat `None`
38.   as "invalid entry" → `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` (L308, L316, L535, L633,
39.   L786, L853, L864).
40. - `unsafe { pd.write(pde_idx, new_pde) }` / `pt.write(pte_idx, new_pte)` to
41.   install freshly-built entries (L320, L583, L665).
42. - The entry-type parameter `E` is fixed per level: PD tables only carry
43.   `PageDirectoryEntry`, PT tables only `PageTableEntry`. The phantom-typed
44.   `Table<E>` is exactly what enforces this at the call sites.
45. 
46. ### 2. UserVM guest page walker — `src/uservm/src/guest_profiler/gva.rs` (host-side)
47. 
48. `translate_gva()` performs a *software* two-level walk over guest memory:
49. 
50. ```rust
51. let pd_index: usize = paging::pd_index(gva as usize).into_raw();
52. let pt_index: usize = paging::pt_index(gva as usize).into_raw();
53. ```

56. bytes are read directly from a host pointer (`read_unaligned`) rather than via
57. `Table::read`, because the guest's memory is not mapped into the host address
58. space. This caller relies *solely* on the index-extraction arithmetic being
59. correct (mask to `[0, PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)`) and on `into_raw` returning that same
60. value unchanged.

1. # View Design: `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`
2. 
3. ## Abstract Resource
4. 
5. To callers this module is **a single hardware page-table page**: a fixed-length
6. array of `PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` (= 1024) typed entries, addressed by a *validated*
7. in-range index (`TableIndex`) and backed by volatile, caller-owned memory at a
8. physical/identity-mapped base address.
9. 
10. Abstractly it is a **partial map `index → Option<E>`** over one page, plus two
11. pure helpers (`pd_index`, `pt_index`) that extract the directory/table index of
12. a virtual address. The phantom type `E` keeps PD and PT pages from being mixed.
13. 
14. Two types need abstraction:
15. 
16. | Type | What it is to a caller |
17. |------|------------------------|
18. | `TableIndex` | a *validated* slot number, guaranteed `< PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` |
19. | `Table<E>` | a typed, non-owning handle whose observable content is the per-slot entry map |
20. 
21. ---
22. 
23. ## View Structs
24. 
25. ### `TableIndex`
26. 
27. A `TableIndex` carries exactly one piece of caller-visible information: the
28. validated index value. Its abstract value is a single `nat`.
29. 
30. ```rust
31. impl View for TableIndex {
32.     type V = nat;
33.     // value returned by into_raw(); always < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH (see inv)
34.     pub closed spec fn view(&self) -> nat;
35. }
36. ```
37. 
38. ### `Table<E>`
39. 
40. ```rust
41. pub struct TableView<E: TableEntry> {
42.     /// Physical/identity-mapped base address this handle denotes.
43.     /// Caller-meaningful identity: which page read/write act on.
44.     pub addr: nat,
45.     /// Logical contents: the entry a `read` would return for each valid slot.
46.     /// `entries[i] == None` means slot `i` holds a word that is not a valid
47.     /// encoding of `E`; `Some(e)` (including a not-present, zeroed entry) is a
48.     /// valid decode.
49.     pub entries: Map<nat, Option<E>>,
50. }
51. 
52. impl View for Table<E> {
53.     type V = TableView<E>;
54.     pub closed spec fn view(&self) -> TableView<E>;
55. }
56. ```
57. 
58. `E: TableEntry` is `Copy`; the trait supplies two pure spec projections used by
59. the transitions below (their `requires`/`ensures` are designed in the spec
60. phase; `raw`/`from_raw` are in verification scope, so these are *proven*, not
61. assumed):
62. 
63. ```rust
64. spec fn spec_raw(self: E) -> PteWord;              // serialize
65. spec fn spec_from_raw(w: PteWord) -> Option<E>;    // decode (None = invalid)
66. ```
67. 
68. with the round-trip **trait law** `spec_from_raw(e.spec_raw()) == Some(e)`.
69. 
70. ---
71. 
72. ## Well-formedness Invariants
73. 
74. ```rust
75. // TableIndex: the validated-range guarantee callers depend on.
76. pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {     // on TableIndex
77.     self@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH
78. }
79. ```
80. 
81. ```rust
82. impl<E: TableEntry> TableView<E> {
83.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
84.         // exactly one page worth of slots, no more, no fewer
85.         &&& self.entries.dom() =~= Set::new(|i: nat| i < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)
86.         // a page-table page is page-aligned
87.         &&& self.addr % PAGE_SIZE == 0
88.     }
89. }
90. ```
91. 
92. The `Table` type-level `inv()` is `self@.inv()`.
93. 
94. ---
95. 
96. ## Spec Transition Functions
97. 
98. ### Pure index extractors (produce a `TableIndex` value = `nat`)
99. 
100. ```rust
101. pub open spec fn spec_table_index(vaddr: nat, shift: nat) -> nat {
102.     (vaddr >> shift) & (PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1)        // low 10 bits after shift
103. }
104. pub open spec fn spec_pd_index(vaddr: nat) -> nat { spec_table_index(vaddr, PGTAB_SHIFT) }
105. pub open spec fn spec_pt_index(vaddr: nat) -> nat { spec_table_index(vaddr, PAGE_SHIFT) }
106. ```
107. 
108. - `pd_index(vaddr)` → `result@ == spec_pd_index(vaddr as nat)` (and `inv`, i.e.
109.   `result@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, which follows from the mask).
110. - `pt_index(vaddr)` → `result@ == spec_pt_index(vaddr as nat)` (and `inv`).
111. - `TableIndex::into_raw(self)` → `result == self@` (identity projection).
112. - `TableIndex::new(i)` → `Some(t)` iff `i < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, and then
113.   `t@ == i`; `None` otherwise. *(out of stated scope, but specifiable.)*
114. 
115. ### Handle creation
116. 
117. ```rust
118. // from_address only fixes identity; contents are pre-existing memory.
119. pub open spec fn spec_from_address(base: nat) -> /* addr field of */ nat { base }
120. ```
121. 
122. - `Table::from_address(base)` → `result@.addr == base`. `entries` are left
123.   unconstrained: they reflect whatever the backing page already holds.
124. 
125. ### Read / write (the `index → Option<E>` map)
126. 
127. ```rust
128. impl<E: TableEntry> TableView<E> {
129.     pub open spec fn spec_read(self, idx: nat) -> Option<E> {
130.         self.entries[idx]
131.     }
132.     pub open spec fn spec_write(self, idx: nat, entry: E) -> TableView<E> {
133.         TableView {
134.             entries: self.entries.insert(idx, E::spec_from_raw(entry.spec_raw())),
135.             ..self                              // frame: addr unchanged
136.         }
137.     }
138. }
139. ```
140. 
141. - `Table::read(&self, index)` → `result == self@.spec_read(index@)`
142.   (requires `index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, met by `TableIndex::inv`).
143. - `Table::write(&self, index, entry)` →
144.   `self@ == old(self)@.spec_write(index@, entry)` — only slot `index@` changes,
145.   `addr` and every other slot are preserved by `..self` / `insert`.
146. 
147. **Read-after-write** falls out directly:
148. `spec_read(spec_write(s, i, e), i) == spec_from_raw(e.spec_raw())`, and by the
149. trait round-trip law this is `Some(e)`. Writes to `j != i` leave slot `i`
150. untouched because `Map::insert` only alters the keyed slot.
151. 
152. ---
153. 
154. ## Design Rationale (per field, with substitution test)
155. 
156. > Substitution test: *if the implementation were rewritten with a different
157. > algorithm, would this field still make sense?*
158. 
159. ### `TableIndex@ : nat`
160. - **Why:** the only thing every caller asks of a `TableIndex` is its numeric
161.   value and the promise it is `< PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`. `gva.rs` does
162.   `into_raw().checked_mul(entry_size)` relying on that bound; `identity_map.rs`
163.   feeds it straight to `read`/`write`.
164. - **Substitution:** ✅ Any representation (newtype over `usize`, a `u16`, a
165.   bitfield slice) still denotes one index value. `nat` is the algorithm-free
166.   essence; `into_raw` is its identity projection.
167. 
168. ### `TableView::addr : nat`

170.   denotes the page at `base`.”* Callers build PD/PT handles from physical
171.   addresses they computed and must know the handle refers to that page.
172. - **Substitution:** ✅ Any handle to a page-table page must know which page it
173.   addresses, regardless of how it stores it. (The `PhantomData` marker, by
174.   contrast, is pure implementation and is excluded — see Rejected.)
175.

 ## Abstract Resource
 
 To callers this module is **a single hardware page-table page**: a fixed-length
 array of `PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` (= 1024) typed entries, addressed by a *validated*
 in-range index (`TableIndex`) and backed by volatile, caller-owned memory at a
 physical/identity-mapped base address.

 pure helpers (`pd_index`, `pt_index`) that extract the directory/table index of
 a virtual address. The phantom type `E` keeps PD and PT pages from being mixed.
 
 Two types need abstraction:
 
 | Type | What it is to a caller |
 |------|------------------------|
 | `TableIndex` | a *validated* slot number, guaranteed `< PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` |
 | `Table<E>` | a typed, non-owning handle whose observable content is the per-slot entry map |

 ### `TableIndex`
 
 A `TableIndex` carries exactly one piece of caller-visible information: the
 validated index value. Its abstract value is a single `nat`.
 
 ```rust
 impl View for TableIndex {
     type V = nat;
     // value returned by into_raw(); always < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH (see inv)
     pub closed spec fn view(&self) -> nat;
 }
 ```
 
 ### `Table<E>`
 
 ```rust

     /// Physical/identity-mapped base address this handle denotes.
     /// Caller-meaningful identity: which page read/write act on.
     pub addr: nat,
     /// Logical contents: the entry a `read` would return for each valid slot.
     /// `entries[i] == None` means slot `i` holds a word that is not a valid
     /// encoding of `E`; `Some(e)` (including a not-present, zeroed entry) is a
     /// valid decode.
     pub entries: Map<nat, Option<E>>,

     type V = TableView<E>;
     pub closed spec fn view(&self) -> TableView<E>;
 }
 ```

 the transitions below (their `requires`/`ensures` are designed in the spec
 phase; `raw`/`from_raw` are in verification scope, so these are *proven*, not
